turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: what brought you in today?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I'm just having a lot of chest pain, and so I thought I should get it checked out.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And before we start, could you remind me of your gender and age?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. 39. I'm a male.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. OK. And so when did this chest pain start?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: It started last night, but it's becoming sharper.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And where is this pain located?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: It's located on the last side of my chest.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And so how long has it been going on for or then if it started last night?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: So I guess it would be a couple of hours now, maybe like eight.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Has it been constant throughout that time or changing?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I would say it's been pretty constant, yeah.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And how would you describe the pain?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: People will use words sometimes like sharp burning, achy. I'd say it's pretty sharp, yeah. It's sharp.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Anything that you have done since last night that's made the pain better?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Not laying down, helps. OK. So do you find laying down makes the pain worse?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes. Definitely.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Do you find that the pain is radiating anywhere?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Is there anything else that makes the pain worse besides laying down?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Not that I've noticed, no. OK. So not like taking a deep breath or anything like that?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Maybe taking a deep breath. Yeah.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And one of the pains started, could you tell you, could you think of anything that you were doing at the time?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I mean, I was moving some furniture around, but that I've done that before.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. So you didn't feel like you hurt yourself when you were doing that?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And in regards to how severe the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10, 10 being the worst pain you've ever felt, how severe would you say the pain is?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'd say it's like a seven or eight. Pretty bad.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And with the pain, do you have any other associated symptoms?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I feel a little lightheaded, and I'm having some trouble breathing.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Have you had any loss of consciousness?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Have you been experiencing any, like, racing of the heart?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: A little bit, yeah.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And have you been sweaty at all?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Just from the shirt, just from having issues breathing. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Have you been having issues breathing since the pain started?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And recently, have you had any periods of time where you have been immobilized or you haven't been able to move around a lot?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. OK. And have you been feeling sick at all, any infectious symptoms?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Have you had any nausea or vomiting?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Any fevers or chills?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. How about any abdominal pain?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Any urinary problems?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Or bowel problems?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Have you had a cough?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. You haven't brought up any blood?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: You've got a cough?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Have you had a wheeze with your difficulty breathing?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. Not that I've heard. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Any changes to the breath sounds at all?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Like, any noisy breathing?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Well, I guess, when I'm really having trouble breathing, yeah.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Has anything like this ever happened to you before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And have you had any night sweats?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: All right. And then how about any rashes or skin changes?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No rashes. But I guess, like, my neck seems to be a little swollen. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Do you have any neck pain?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Have you had any, like, accidents, like a car accident or anything where you really jerked your neck?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Any trauma at all to the chest or back?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: OK. So just in regards to past medical history,

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: do you have any prior medical conditions?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Any recent hospitalizations?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Any prior surgeries?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Do you take any medications regularly?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Are they prescribed or over the counter?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: No. All right. How about any allergies to medications?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: None.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: All right. Any immunizations?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Or are they up to date?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: They're all up to date. Excellent. All right. And could you tell me a little bit about your living situation currently?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I live in an apartment by myself. Yep. That's about it. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: And how do you support yourself financially?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'm going to count in. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Sounds like a pretty stressful job. Or that it can be. Do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I do.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And how much do you smoke?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Smoke about a pack a day. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: How long have you been smoking for?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: For the past 10 to 15 years. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: And do you smoke cannabis?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sometimes.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: How much marijuana would you smoke per week?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Per week?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Maybe about five milligrams, not that much.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: And do you use any other recreational drugs?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Like cocaine, crystal meth, opioids?

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: No. OK. Have you used IV drugs before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: And do you drink alcohol?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I do. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: How much alcohol do you drink each week?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: About I have like one or two drinks a day. So about 10 drinks a week.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And then briefly could you tell me a little bit about your diet and exercise?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I try to eat healthy for dinner at least, but most of my lunches are I eat out. And then in terms of exercise, I try to exercise every other day. I run for about half an hour. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Oh, that's great.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: They're driven working on the activity and the diets as well.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: So has anything like this happened in your family before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. Has anybody in the family had a heart attack before?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Actually, yes. My father had a heart attack when he was 45.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And anybody in the family have cholesterol problems?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I think my father did. I see.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And how about anybody in the family have stroke?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No strokes.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: OK. And then any cancers in the family?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. OK.

turns.speaker: CLINICIAN
turns.text: Was there anything else that you wanted to tell me about today that on history?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No. I don't think so. I think you asked me everything.
